newsitem.title: CHINA: China futures exchange tightens grip on hedging.
newsitem.headline: China futures exchange tightens grip on hedging.

text.p: The China Commodity Futures Exchange in southern Hainan province has issued rules to boost controls on hedging trade to reduce risk, the Futures Herald said on Wednesday.
The exchange mainly trades natural rubber and coffee contracts.
The exchange required firms and traders to follow strict procedures in applications for hedging positions, the newspaper said.
Only manufacturers and dealers in commodities related to hedging contracts were allowed to take part in the business, it said.
Traders could only use their hedging positions for spot delivery and liquidation, it said.
The exchange would closely monitor traders on their hedging transactions and vowed to punish violators who broke the rules, the newspaper said.
China has been promoting hedging in its fledgling futures market to provide the opportunity for manufacturers to offset risk.
